quotes.excerpt: Beast of Borikén #1 is the kind of story that delivers on multiple levels, a frightening monster tale while also offering much more beneath the surface. Julio Anta and Daniel Irizarri craft a coin that blends folklore and horror with community and identity into something truly compelling. Beast of Boriken is a haunting and heartfelt reimagining of the Chupacabra that proves some of the most powerful monsters are often in real-world struggles.

Great start to this series; I thoroughly enjoyed this first issue from start to finish. The story is easy to follow and relatable considering that it has several themes such as: environmental preservation, ancestral duty, the death of a loved one, and the appearance of a strange creature amongst the rubble. I think lovers of indie comics will love this one, as it’s a change of pace from the superhero genre. The artwork shines and matches well with the compact yet detailed dialogue from the characters. The beast’s design is memorable.

The things that Haun and his team are doing are truly electric and terrifying. “Dooney Hollow” is for those that love slow burn horror with plenty of mystery and fall vibes. If you want that, then you need to pick this up!

The Folk of Dooney Hollow #1 is a compelling horror debut that pairs a steadily unfolding mystery with atmospheric artwork and an unsettling Ozark setting. Its strong pacing, memorable final reveal, and lingering unanswered questions make the next issue an easy recommendation. Make sure to pick a copy of this first issue up when you are at the shop this week. Also, well you are there, you should just add this to your Pull List as I’m confident that you will want more of this amazing and eerie world.

The Dirt Beneath the Devil #1 is an amazing opening issue for the series that will surely trap readers’ interest in reading more of the series. The mysteries that this issue either straight out tells us or implies are enough to peek even the most jaded readers’ interest. The premise that is laid out here in the first issue is intriguing, but when you know that Panosian obviously has more in store for us that jacks the intrigued levels all the way up. This should be a slam dunk pick up at the shop or Neon Ichiban this week. As a matter of fact, make sure to add this one to your Pull List as you won’t want to miss a single issue of this series.
The Dirt Beneath the Devil #1 is a solid debut issue. It takes a familiar concept and puts it in a setting that feels rather new and fresh.

Killer Influences #1 stands out by blending societies true crime obsession with influencer culture in a way that feels both unsettling and original. Joey Esposito crafts a chilling tale, while Valeria Burzo and Iñaki Azpiazu really bring the story together with excellent illustrations and color. Killer Influences is a gripping true crime story turning fame and fear into a dangerously addictive pact.

All in all, fans of dark comedy and true crime will find Killer Influences bloody hilarious. More sensitive souls need not apply. However, if you’re a fan of Only Murders in the Building, this will be up your alley.

I wasn’t sure how these self-contained issues would work in a world where we’ve gotten used to 3-5 issue arcs, but man, have they been fun. Last issue, it was Reed and Johnny sent back to Rome, now we’ve got sibling hijinks. This issue was fun, entertaining, and just an all around great Fantastic Four story.

Fantastic Four #13 is another reminder that Ryan North understands exactly what makes Marvel's First Family so compelling: their powers are tools for creativity as much as they are instruments of heroism. Anchored by a wonderfully absurd premise, the issue balances humor, tension, and character dynamics with remarkable ease. Andrea Sorrentino and Edgar Delgado elevate the material with visuals that lean into horror without sacrificing the fun at the story's core. The result is a memorable one-shot that showcases both the elasticity of the Fantastic Four concept and the joy of watching creators push familiar characters into unexpected territory.

There are some great visuals by Bengal here, with a base Selina keeps in the mountains being especially impressive. The pace only speeds up this issue, and the characters added to this story continue to pull you in.

Absolute Catwoman #2 takes us into Selena’s past tying it all together as the mystery begins to unfold. I’m enjoying what Che, Bengal, Giovanna, Scott, and Lucas are putting together which is letting Selena have her time to shine. I’ll continue to pick this book up for sure.

Void Rivals 33 was a tremendous showcase of everything that is possible with this series as the creative team keeps finding new ways to keep this title every bit as entertaining as its fellow bigger name Energon Universe pillars.

Rom makes his presence known early in a solid showcase issue. Kirkman welcomes the Space Knight into the EU with a great script. Hughes and Delpeche capture some mystery behind the noble actions with strong art. Get ready for another excellent addition to comics’ most unpredictable universe!

The Brutal Dark is poised to strike but Ezra Cain is flying into the heart of danger in this exciting chapter. Condon wraps up events  with a direct shot of intensity. Phillips’ art takes readers on a roller-coaster ride of emotions.  A great “so long for now”, but definitely not “goodbye forever”.
While the finale feels a little abrupt, Peril of the Brutal Dark: An Ezra Cain Mystery #6 is still a great final issue for one of the best series of the year.
G.I. Joe #25 is a major milestone done right, paying off years of buildup and kicking off the series' most epic storyline yet.

G.I. JOE #25 is a phenomenal start to the Nightforce story arc. Joshua Williamson, Tom Reilly and Andrea Milana pace things out that you feel like you are experiencing the start of a big blockbuster event. Everything that happens in this issue comes across as being a payoff for many sub-plots that have been developed since the start of the series. Where the payoff leads to is anyone’s guess, leaving you as the reader even more excited to find out what happens next.

Superman #40 is damn near perfect. This arc acted as a bit of a redemption for Superboy Prime and I absolutely adore him after this. Whilst the story here is wrapped up, this isn’t the last time we will see Superboy Prime and there seems to be a bright future ahead for him and his “supporting characters”.

This has been a phenomenal story setting up Prime’s future, but special credit once again goes to Dan Mora, who plays with the nature of the comic book format in some incredibly unique ways. The original Superman is back next month for the kickoff of the big “Kingdom of Zod” event, but I hope Williamson gets to keep writing Prime for a long time.

Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles #300 (#20) not only pushes the great story that we have been following forward, but also gives this milestone issue a big feel as well. The drama, action, surprises, and emotions are firing on all cylinders in this issue. If this issue doesn’t make you feel something you may need to check your pulse. They could’ve just phoned this one in as the 300th issue milestone is more than enough to sell the book. But they didn’t phone it in at all and crafted an issue that is sure to bring readers back next month for issue 21. If Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles is not on your Pull List already it needs to be added ASAP! If you are a comic book collector this 300th issue needs to be added to your collection as well. Cheers to 300 issues of TMNT and can’t wait for the 400th milestone issue!

This issue takes you on an emotional ride! Sure there is plenty of action within these pages. All while tugging at your heart strings with the current situation revolving around Shen. Losing a loved one and having the chance to bring them back is going to hit home with many readers I suspect. You do not want to miss out on this start of a new storyline for this series of TMNT. Go get your copy today!
Power Rangers Unlimited #1 is a bold, legacy embracing start which easily grabs hold of the best of BOOM!-era Power Rangers comics and presents it from a fresh and exciting angle.

Power Rangers Unlimited #1 delivers an action-packed debut that leans into Power Rangers history from a fresh point of view, and when combined with the out-of-this-world art and extensive roster, Power Rangers Unlimited becomes a must-read for any and every fan of the franchise.

Operation: Iron Coffin #2 keeps the momentum going with a bigger, bloodier, and more personal chapter for Dracula. Kenny Porter deepens the story without slowing down the action, while Tyrell Cannon’s artwork delivers the chaos, horror, and energy this concept demands. This series continues to be an absolute blast and remains an easy Pull List recommendation. Do not sleep on this series! Make sure you jump on this train now, as you don’t want to miss what happens next.

I don’t know how they’re doing it, but “Operation: Iron Coffin” is one of the best out this year. Kenny Porter manages to create a version of Dracula that feels relatable yet horrifying. His writing coupled with Cannon’s fantastic artwork create a truly amazing reading experience.
One of the best series in comics right now. The art is wild, creative, adventurous, and stunning. The story keeps drawing you back in issue after issue.
Marc Spector: Moon Knight #7 delivers an exhilarating ride with huge action, incredible artwork, and deadly stakes. It leaves you itching for the next issue.

The Smart Division is a fantastic science-fiction mystery that eerily could be more fact than fiction. Writer Zack Kaplan delivers a timely detective tale exploring the use of modern technology in solving crimes. However, it’s the juxtaposition of John Pearson’s elegant brush strokes that makes story rise above the rest. Kaplan and Pearson’s creativity knows no bounds and The Smart Division is proof of that.

I sat down with The Smart Division expecting a slick sci-fi detective story and walked away rattled about the world outside my window. That is the highest thing I can say about a comic right now. This is a perfect debut and one of the most relevant books on the stands, and I cannot wait to see where the case goes.

King Shazam and Superman throw down in a final fight for the ages! Arron leaves it all on table with the script. The art team never knows a ceiling in how far to raise the stakes. Highest possible recommendation.

Absolute Superman #21 feels like a true spectacle and lives up to the hype in every way as this arc comes to. a close. There is so much violence, emotion, and power packed into these pages that it may, in fact, be my favorite issue of the run yet.

Operation: Iron Coffin comes out of the gate swinging with a unique premise that delivers far more than ever expected. Kenny Porter and Tyrell Cannon give us a Dracula that isn’t just here for the carnage, although we get plenty of that, but for a compelling redemption arc wrapped in a fast-paced, blood-soaked WWII setting. IDW Dark may have some heavy hitting titles in its first year as an imprint at IDW Publishing, but Operation: Iron Coffin stands out as one of the best.

Operation Coffin #1 is a stylish debut for Porter and Cannon’s new take on Dracula. A truly unique premise, backed by engaging lore and a curious mission have already laid the groundwork for a wild ride ahead.

We get our first hints of how this fits in with the rest of the Absolute Universe just as it ends, but this feels much more like an evergreen, one-of-a-kind comic that people will be talking about for years.

Camp, Rodríguez and Otsmane-Elhaou leave readers with an intense read unlike anything else seen in the comics landscape currently. A phenomenal script gels perfectly with Rodríguez’s incredible art yet again. While its’ a bittersweet moment with the series on hold/over, readers leave with an overwhelming sense of the true direction of superhero comics for years to come. Highest possible recommendation.
Superman: The Stranger #1 returns to Clark Kent's roots, spinning a story that shows why Superman is such a timeless character.

The best Superman comic I’ve read in years!  A 1930s reinvention of the Man of Steel that returns Superman to his 1930s roots, but zigs and zags in ways you won’t expect, while keeping you on your toes. With a story that hooks you from the go and art and colours that leap off the page, this is a must-read mini-series.

Six of Us #1 turns a seemingly perfect 1990s sitcom cast into a web of secrets, resentment, and murder, with Tom King and Gabriel Hernández Walta delivering a compelling mystery that leaves everyone looking potentially guilty.

SIX OF US reminds us why this award winning creative team is so unstoppable. It's a human story about the importance of creating art, but the cost of it too. Six of Us #1 invites us to consider what true fulfillment looks like, and whether it has anything to do with success.

The Kingdom has fallen but long live the King? That is the question posed in this latest chapter. Williamson sets the stage for an epic finale. The art team captures the personal toll taken as one more attack looks to bring the house down, ready for not. A crossover event living up to the marque billing.
Superman #42 is less an important issue and more of a stopgap as it builds up the finale of the Kingdom of Zod storyline. Hopefully, that finale is worth the wait.

The Fast Food life has caught up with Kyle Rayner at a most inopportune time. Adams nails the laughs while staging the more serious points. The art teams leave nothign to chance with the action. This is a story that can only be told in the pages of Green Lantern.

Green Lantern #39 is a fun conclusion to this strange little food fight, but the Kyle Rayner/Major Force confrontation is the real meal of the issue. Adams continues to show that Kyle’s history matters, and seeing him confront Major Force with a little more maturity gives their rivalry a fresh dimension. The food comedy may be a bit much at times, but the character work, art, Jade’s continued presence, and setup for “First Light” leave me excited for what comes next.
Void Rivals #34 breaks from the series' usual slow-burn pacing to deliver a tightly contained, action-packed chapter featuring standout art from Conor Hughes and a game-changing cliffhanger.

Rom’s arrival isn’t with strings or a bounty attatched in this action packed issue. Kirkman delivers on quite a throwdown with the writing. Hughes and Delpeche keep the energetic art shining right to the end. The addition of Rom to the EU is paying instant dividends.
Justice League Unlimited #23 delivers a major battle, an argument that could tear the group apart, and the tease of a twist that could have substantial ramifications.

FINAL GRADE:  7Harley Quinn enters “Bad Seeds” with a routine entrance, playing to her strengths as a character. Kalan hits key points while using this as a stepping stone for a greater meeting. The art & lettering match the madcap style of Quinn’s life for a great fit. Expect more fireworks next time around.

This issue raises an ethical dilemma in a more light-hearted manner; however, the main point is not lost on the audience. This team continues to cook with this Flash run, and every issue builds upon the one before it so well.

Wally West’s dreams turn into nightmares as the Justice League weighs in on his latest movement. North stages the ethics debate with a well structured script. Guidry and Lucas present the unique visions with excellent imagery. With great ambition comes grave consequences for the Scarlet Speedster. Don’t miss it.

Even with the set up happening in a different series, Detective Comics #1113 is such a near perfect Batman adventure that it could convince even the most cash-strapped bat-fans to add it to their pulls.

Batman takes to the skies to save his city in a thrilling addition to “Bad Seeds”! Taylor throws a daring rescue attempt in Bat’s direction with great success. Spokes jumps in and keeps the excitement running high all issue long. In Gotham’s darkest hour, Batman is still bringing the fight in its’ honor.

The Finest meet the Harbingers in a great opening round of the latest arc! Waid crafts the dangerous plans of Al Ghul with a magnificent start. Gutiérrez & the team deliver a thrilling journey into the fight for survival. World’s Finest is always a safe bet to deliver each time out!

Batman/Superman: World’s Finest #55 launches its new arc with the huge superhero spectacle this series does so well. Mark Waid wastes little time establishing Ra’s al Ghul’s terrifying plan, while Adrián Gutiérrez keeps the action fast, inventive, and appropriately dangerous. The villain team-up adds an unpredictable element, and the rapidly escalating global threat gives this opening chapter the scale of a full-blown event.
Catwoman #91 brings empathy and a heist to the Bad Seeds event making for an intriguing angle as the stories slowly set up to converge!
Catwoman #91 ties the series into Batman: Bad Seeds in an organic, compelling way while also providing moments of genuine character growth.

King’s plot has been long and winding. The overarching story that's taken so long to reach this particular point has been spotty at best. There are occasional issues that feel very weak and occasional treatments of classic ideas that also feel very weak. However, the overall story that King is jamming into place begins to feel like a little bit more of an accomplishment with each issue. It hasn't exactly been a graceful journey. However, it does begin to feel like.King is going to be able to tell a compelling story featuring Wonder Woman that continues t hrough her 85th birthday next month.
Wonder Woman #37 expertly balances foreshadowing and top notch action to deliver a blockbuster beginning to the second part of the "Wonder War" story arc.

I’ll sound like a broken record but if you haven’t dived into this run, what are you waiting for?! Every arc is somehow better than the last. The character’s development is making huge changes that’ll go down in X-Men history. The stories will have you hooked onto every page. Plus, the creative team makes this entire issue a feast for the eyes. The Uncanny X-Men #35 continues that impossibly high quality that we’re so used to seeing in this run.

The demons within strike Rogue and Gambit as his curse worsens in this latest chapter! Simone locks in on their struggles while staging Howler’s storyline in a new direction. Vecchio and Wilson deliver a showcase of action and drama between the panels. This series keeps redefining what X-Men stories should be!

This new story arc for the TMNT Universe is proving to be a challenge that they were warned would happen. I can understand wanting both of your parents back, but at the cost of New York City… This team continues to produce amazing issues every month with great action and storytelling. The added Chinese lore to this series is a joy to see. Seeing the Turtles engage in their heritage is something people should mimic. Take pride in your roots and where you come from. This is a great series and a great read for TMNT and non-TMNT fans.

Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles #22 delivers an exciting escalation of The City That Never Dies, combining supernatural mystery, family consequences, and clear, atmospheric artwork. Gene Luen Yang, Fero Pe, and Luis Antonio Delgado turn Obon into the backdrop for a compelling catastrophe, leaving the Turtles facing a larger and more personal threat. It is a strong, fast-moving issue that builds anticipation for what comes next.

reason.snippet: The vast cast Christopher Priest has built over the years are all on seemingly separate journeys in Vampirella #6 as each looks for clarity and meaning.
pros: Davis Goetten's character expressions and gesture work are superb, allowing the quieter scenes to really resonate.
Color artist Giovanni Caputo's color work is really shown off this issue with impressive use of lighting.
Christopher Priest's scripting remains great, with a good use of tension.
cons: The scenes here all work, but the book itself feels disjointed. Momentum doesn't build between scenes.

reason.label: AIPT review
reason.snippet: Feral #26 is a character-driven issue which explores Elsie’s insecurities and self-doubt. By examining the character’s anxieties, the reader is able to see Elsie at her most sympathetic and identifiable. Elsie’s feeling that she is not good enough is an all too common feeling for so many of us, and it’s what makes Elsie so relatable and endearing in this issue.
pros: Great character work exploring Elsie and her anxieties
This issue sets up an exciting new chapter in the ongoing saga that is Feral
Jam-packed with lots of fantastic artwork from Trish Forstner, Tone Rodriguez, and Brad Simpson

reason.label: AIPT review
reason.snippet: What Burnham, Schoening, Myer and Delgado have done on this series for 40+ issues is nothing short of amazing. So many lifelong TMNT fans were introduced to these characters through the 1987 cartoon and they've absolutely done those fans proud. They consistently delivered the kind of energetic, heartfelt and genuinely funny adventures that made this version of the Turtles so memorable in the first…
pros: A fitting and heartfelt finale that gives the series a proper sendoff while leaving the door open for future adventures.
Sarah Myer delivers standout artwork, with expressive character work, exciting action sequences, and memorable villain designs.
A celebration of the 1987 TMNT legacy that combines the humor, heart, and colorful fun of the cartoon.
cons: The central rescue plot is fairly straightforward, relying on familiar tropes even if Burnham adds some nice character moments.

reason.label: AIPT review
reason.snippet: The fight between Bishop and Mirrormind doesn't really work, leading to a flat feeling. An interesting reveal at the end just makes you yearn for that to have been the main plot of the series.
pros: All three artists do well in their sections.
The end reveal sets up an interesting conflict for the finale.
cons: Federica Mancin's art stands out in a way that feels jarring, especially after a rhythm built in previous issues.
The reveal at the end highlights the lack of stakes in the previous issues.
The fight with Mirrormind is surprisingly unimaginative.

reason.label: AIPT review
reason.snippet: Gambit Gone #1 gets plenty of mileage out of its two Remy LeBeaus, using their different histories to set up parallel questions of guilt and redemption. The opening Sentinel battle is the highlight, delivering real danger and a great showcase for Edoardo Audino, while Earth-295's roaming Krakoa is an inspired addition to the Age of Apocalypse. The issue loses some energy once exposition takes over…
pros: The two Gambits create an interesting opportunity to examine Remy from different perspectives
Excellent opening battle establishes the stakes immediately
Earth-295's walking Krakoa is a fantastic concept
Audino and Gerardo Sandoval give the two universes distinct visual identities
cons: Exposition slows the story after the strong opening
The Gambit and Vig fight runs longer than its narrative importance warrants

reason.label: AIPT review
reason.snippet: Superman: Father of Tomorrow #5 builds to a literally explosive climax, which showing how certain characters' hubris is their eventual downfall. When all's said and done, this is shaping up to be an Elseworlds that I'll wholeheartedly recommend to all kinds of Superman fans.
pros: Porter slowly reveals how certain characters' hubris is setting the stage for their downfall.
Earls draws a hell of a fight between Luthor, Lane, and Jor-El.
A literally explosive ending that sets the stage for the final issue.
This is shaping up to be an Elseworlds fans need to check out.

reason.label: AIPT review
reason.snippet: Justice League Unlimited #23 delivers a major battle, an argument that could tear the group apart, and the tease of a twist that could have substantial ramifications.
pros: Waid's story meshes an ideological argument with an intense fight, which could both have significant consequences.
Mora's art captures both the battle and the heated confrontation in a way that makes it feel like a boxing fight between two heavyweights.
Bonvillain continues to utilize a wide range of colors to complement the fantastic nature of the story, as seen in the battle on Dronnda.
cons: It's nitpicking, but one of the few negatives is the reader's impatience; this issue is another building block, so the audience has to keep waiting for the clim…
The tension in the fight between Luthor and Batman is undercut by pivoting to the battle between the Leaguers and the villains over the powerbank.

reason.label: AIPT review
reason.snippet: Miles Morales: Spider-Man #2 is a near-perfect sophmore issue, exploring how the young web-slinger and his father are dealing with the weight of their own flaws. It also continues to build up Revenant as a more than worthy foe for Miles, thanks to their personal connection.
pros: Hill touches on the ideas of accepting your flaws, which is fitting given the narrative.
De Landro and Leon bring their own unique artistic flair to the past and present sequences alike.
Valenza's colors draw a sharp divide between past and present.
Revenant is a very scary, yet worthy foe for Miles.
cons: The dynamic between Miles and Valentina needs more time to grow.

reason.label: AIPT review
reason.snippet: Superman #42 is less an important issue and more of a stopgap as it builds up the finale of the Kingdom of Zod storyline. Hopefully, that finale is worth the wait.
pros: Barrows and Panscia deliver images that are worthy of a Superman book.
The small character moments Williamson brings to the table are a reminder of how great he is writing Superman.
cons: The back half is less storytelling and more build up.
What's the point of bringing young Zod back when Ursa or current day Zod would have been a proper threat?

reason.label: AIPT review
reason.snippet: The Muppets Take the Marvel Universe #1 understands exactly why this crossover works. The creators capture the Muppets' chaotic comedic rhythm while finding clever ways to make Marvel's heroes part of the joke. Chip Zdarsky and Pete Woods deliver an excellent centerpiece, and the shorter stories keep finding new combinations that feel natural, from Wolverine enduring the Electric Mayhem to the Swe…
pros: The Muppets' voices and comedic timing feel authentic throughout
Zdarsky and Woods kick things off with an excellent 25-page centerpiece
Inspired character pairings create some genuinely funny interactions
"Muppets Assemble!" provides a perfect closing gag
cons: The shorter stories naturally have less room to develop their premises

reason.label: AIPT review
reason.snippet: Sleepy Hollow: The Witches of Western Wood #5 ends Sarah Archer's tale in a tide of blood, revenge, and shattered family bonds.
pros: Jaro fills each page with disturbing imagery, most notably a row of severed heads.
Horchar's color art drenches whole pages in shadows, slowly letting in light and revealing the horrors within.
Dawson's script highlights the true horror of this miniseries, which is Sarah's refusal to let her sister go.
A perfect read for fans of Sleepy Hollow or those who want to get in the Halloween spirit.

reason.label: AIPT review
reason.snippet: Gargoyles #2 is a sophomore issue packed with moments big and small, but the small ones stand out most. The creative team should definitely keep that in mind for future issues.
pros: The small character moments are the best in this issue.
Gambone and Bevard perfectly captures the mix of moodiness and myth that defines Gargoyles.
Weisman excels when scripting Brooklyn and Katana's clash against Coldstone.
cons: The comic feels a bit overloaded in terms of plot.
